featured_reviews.name: aditi mandloi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Disappointing Experience – Poor Facilities and Unresponsive Management
I stayed at The Bombay Home Company for a week, and unfortunately, it was one of the most frustrating hospitality experiences I’ve had.
For the first four days, the air conditioning and jet spray in the bathroom were not functioning — a serious issue given the sweltering summer heat in Mumbai. Despite repeated complaints, the issue remained unresolved. An electrician was sent, but the AC continued to malfunction, leaving me to sleep in an uncomfortably hot room night after night.
After several follow-ups, I was finally offered an alternative accommodation — but it was located 10 kilometers away. No shuttle or assistance was provided for the move, and I had to arrange and pay for transport myself. Upon arrival, I was shocked to find that the new place was not a proper Airbnb apartment, but rather a private room that had been hastily vacated for my stay.
The room reeked of cigarette smoke despite being advertised as non-smoking — a serious concern for someone like me with a smoke allergy. The toilet was unhygienic, the space was extremely cramped, and to make matters worse, the geyser didn’t work. When I reported this, I was told someone would come to fix it, but no one showed up even after an hour.
At that point, I decided to vacate the property and requested a refund for the remaining three days. Not only was my request denied, but the management also stopped responding altogether. When I pointed out that the amenities they failed to provide — working AC, geyser, clean and smoke-free room — were not in line with what was promised, they simply said it was “not in their policy” to offer refunds.
The overall experience was deeply disappointing — from the lack of basic amenities to the unprofessional and indifferent attitude of the staff. I would not recommend this place to anyone looking for a comfortable or reliable stay in Mumbai.

Also their sofa had a hole and nail in it which was not visible and i got hurt by that.

featured_reviews.name: Janie Joy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Title: Exceptional Stay at Omkar Vive, Mumbai!

We recently had the pleasure of staying at Omkar Vive in Mumbai, and we were thoroughly impressed with our apartment accommodation. From the moment we arrived, we felt at home, thanks to the thoughtful amenities and services provided.

The apartment was fully equipped with everything we needed, from essentials like shampoo and dishwasher liquid to luxuries like coffee and a washing machine. The AC and fans kept us cool, and the big fans and ac dried our clothes quickly – a huge plus for us!

As a couple unfamiliar with the country, we appreciated the exceptional service offered by Omkar Vive. The complimentary cleaning services were a great touch, and the privacy we received was top-notch. The security cameras added an extra layer of safety, making us feel secure and at ease.

We were also impressed with the convenience of the delivery services, which brought everything right to our doorstep. The taxi services were equally convenient, with pickups and drop-offs right outside our apartment's main door – a huge relief on rainy days or when we didn't want to wait around in the open.

Overall, we highly recommend Omkar Vive for its outstanding services, affordability, and cleanliness. The staff were friendly and helpful, and the property was well-maintained. We felt like we were in good hands, and we can't wait to stay there again.

G and J from New Zealand 🇳🇿

featured_reviews.name: Jayesh Bhagat
featured_reviews.review_text:
Fort is the oldest business district of Mumbai. Fort was the nerve center of the city during the 18th century. Fort George, built by the East India Company around Bombay Castle gave the area its name. The original financial center of the city, fort is home to institutions such as the Bombay Stock Exchange, Reserve Bank of India and Tata Group.

Nariman Point was developed because of space limitations at Mumbai’s original business district, Fort. Built on land reclaimed from the sea, it is named after Khursheed Framji Nariman, a Parsi visionary. Situated at the extreme southern tip of Marine Drive, the area has some of the most expensive office space in the world and is home to some of India’s premier companies.

￼

The Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) was developed to address Mumbai’s growing need for prime commercial space. Built on marshy land reclaimed from the north side of Mahim Creek, Kurla lies to its east and Bandra to the west. BKC is Mumbai’s newest and fastest growing central business district and is planned to serve Mumbai’s needs for prime commercial space for some time to come.

BKC is home to a large number of multinational and Indian conglomerates as well as schools, healthcare facilities, consulates and more.

￼

As a residential destination BKC offers unmatched convenience and a wealth of premium social facilities. The area is home to Mumbai’s premier international schools and educational institutes. BKC is also a diplomatic hub with over 7 consulates. Leading healthcare institutions such as the Asian Heart Hospital provide the best in healthcare in well provided flagship hospitals.

As the leading central business district in India, many blue chip corporate houses and important regulators are headquartered here with many more on their way.

BKC is the ideal location for consulates as it is close to the airport. With huge spaces to expand their operations; consulates like The British deputy high commission and the US consulate have already shifted their administrative offices to BKC. It’s believed that sooner or later, almost all consulates will shift their operations to BKC.

Seamlessly connected and richly appointed, BKC welcomes the connoisse ur with open arms.

￼

A landmark in planned central business districts, the Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) is the premier corporate destination of India. A futuristic commercial locality, it is designed at par with global CBDs and is one of the key developments powering Mumbai’s resurgence as a financial and business powerhouse.

The Bandra Worli Sea Link is just a short drive away and connects the area seamlessly to commercial areas such as Lower Parel and Worli. Apart from that, the newly inaugurated Santacruz-Chembur Link Road that connects the Western suburbs with the Central is just a 20 minute drive from BKC. Both the international and domestic airports are a 15 minute drive away while the Western Express Highway provides rapid connectivity to the Northern Suburbs

featured_reviews.name: Abhilasha Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
Review for Rustamjee Seasons, BKC

If you’re planning to rent or buy here, I’d strongly say: think twice.

The building looks great on the surface with every amenity listed—gym, pool, squash, TT, yoga rooms—but in practice, it’s a disappointment . Here’s why:
1.	Rigid and impractical rules:
•	Table tennis and squash are restricted with sudden, unclear rules—you can’t just go and play when you want.
•	Gym timings are extremely rigid. Management insists the gym cannot open early because the trainer isn’t available, but ironically, the trainer often shows up an hour late even after the gym has officially opened. Makes no sense.
2.	Amenities without basics:
•	The pool is there, but essential float boards or safety equipment are missing. It’s incomplete and not child-friendly.
3.	Hidden charges everywhere:
•	Even after paying steep rents, almost everything is chargeable—yoga rooms, certain common spaces, and more. Feels unfair and exploitative considering the rent is already high.

On top of this, the hygiene is terrible (toilets stink worse than public ones), lifts are painfully slow, and the management is neither flexible nor approachable. If you’re a tenant, your say is practically zero. Even flat owners don’t have much control since the committee runs on its own agenda. And yes parking is scary-no space to even get into the car-forget your car even being cleaned . I think the list is never ending!

Yes, it’s one of the few residential complexes in BKC, but amenities you can’t use and management you can’t reason with cancel out any advantage.

Verdict: Not worth the rent, not worth the stress. Big no from my side.

Very nonsense, non cooperative staff, despite the extreme delay of 18 months by them, they are demanding late payment charges of AED 30000/- against our upfront up to date payment cleared, ultimately we have to move legally soon against their forceful demand of unofficial panelty. Why she gave them preference I wouldn't know. But I felt insulted and therefore expressed my displeasure over what she did and that it should always be first come first serve. I asked her name and she said Afreen and then asked me to go ahead and do whatever I wanted to. I told her I will. At this point she got infuriated and even asked me to shut up. I left the show without having met one of your representatives.

Disgusting experience to say the least.

owner_posts.post_text:
A home is never just about walls and windows. It's about the trust behind every promise and the moments that begin with a simple handover of keys.
For over 35 years, Kolte Patil has been creating spaces where dreams find an address and families build their future.
Every key handed over carries a promise.
A promise of quality, commitment, and trust.

📍 Sinhgad Road – Where Connectivity Meets Convenience
Experience a lifestyle that keeps you close to Pune’s key destinations, thriving business hubs, educational institutions, and everyday essentials. With seamless connectivity to Kothrud, Swargate, Shivajinagar, Pune Railway Station, and the Mumbai–Bengaluru Highway, Sinhgad Road places you at the center of everything that matters.
Live where every destination feels closer and every day feels more connected.

A home is never just about walls and windows. It's about the trust behind every promise and the moments that begin with a simple handover of keys.
For over 35 years, Kolte Patil has been creating spaces where dreams find an address and families build their future.
Every key handed over carries a promise.
A promise of quality, commitment, and trust.

Good design is also knowing what not to build.
Keeping certain areas open, allowing for air and light to do their job and letting the home feel less contained. We always let nature do the talking, so that none of our spaces feel imposing, but almost like an extension of the environment.​

1991 → Today. One foundation. One promise.
For over three decades, every brick laid, every structure raised, and every community shaped has reflected the trust our customers place in us.
What began in 1991 continues today with the same commitment to quality, integrity, and craftsmanship because great construction is built on more than concrete and steel. It’s built on relationships that stand the test of time.
Thank you for being part of our journey. Here's to building the future, together.

Architecture may define the rooms, but it is daily life that gives them their character.  A favourite chair by the window, conversations that stretch longer than
expected and familiar footsteps in familiar corners.
Over time, these small patterns settle in and the space begins to reflect the people within it.​
​

Once the intent is clear, design begins its work.
Proportion, light and details slowly bring the idea to life. Rooms begin to feel purposeful and spaces invite people to pause, meet or just be. The presence of
good design is experienced in the ease of living.​
​

In the discipline of a blueprint lies the decision about how people will live within a space. It is where intention takes its first form and where imagination becomes something tangible enough to build upon.​

There is a particular clarity to a home before it is lived in. No voices yet, no furniture to define its character, only proportion, air and sunlight setting the tone. It is an invitation and a suggestion of mornings to come and fond memories yet to be made.​
​

For a child, home is the first world they explore. Every room is an invitation to imagine. A sofa becomes a mountain, a hallway a racetrack and a window seat a place to dream. Within these familiar walls, curiosity finds the freedom to wander.​
​

featured_reviews.name: nabamita roy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very bad service. No one should trust them. You need to ask for proof for each and every claim they make as they make several false statements while selling houses. We bought an apartment from them in ivy estate where they made several claims which were all lies and they knew it still they duped the buyers knowingly.

1. They claimed that a road is going to be built connecting ivy estate to kharadi and wagoli main road. None of these were built and instead a wall was erected where road extension was supposed to be.

2. The building quality is bad and there is water seepage issue within a year of handover

3. They said it will all be open parking but alloted parking without taking any permission from owners at the last moment on first come first serve basis. As a result most people have to literally trek to their parking spots.

4. There is no lift in multi storey podium parking.

5. Electrical lines were not laid properly. Lot of electricity problems.

6. They did not install necessary electricity connection to prevent power trips and failures and other issues. The ivy nia housing society had to spend 10 lakhs getting this done which should have been done by the builder.

7. There is a road outside ivy estate that is used by all of the residents there to go to the main road. This road is in an area owned by someone else. Kolte patil builders took the road area on lease for only as long as they were doing construction and selling units in ivy estate. They stopped all payments and did not resolve or prepare proper documentation for the shared road as a result of which ivy estate people have a broken, water logged road which they have to fix out of their own society budget every few days.

8. They claimed they have their own water treatment plant but the water supply is bogus to say the least.

Many more such issues are there. In short they are cheating customers. Think twice before trusting them.
